solution: For the path on m vertices, the Laplacian eigenvalues are 2−2cos(kπ/m), k=0,…,m−1. By the Cartesian-product rule, the 3×5 grid has eigenvalues λ_{a,b}=4−2cos(aπ/3)−2cos(bπ/5), for a=0,1,2 and b=0,…,4. The matrix-tree theorem gives the tree count as (1/15) times the product of the 14 nonzero eigenvalues. Evaluating this product gives 36,225, so the number of spanning trees is 36,225/15 = 2,415.
insight: For a connected graph, the product of its nonzero Laplacian eigenvalues equals its vertex count times its number of spanning trees.
insight_justification: This is the eigenvalue form of the matrix-tree theorem: each principal cofactor of the Laplacian counts spanning trees, and their sum is the product of the nonzero eigenvalues.
